# Codemap - issue 0147, round 14: the pinned gap `equal-to-force-points-limit-border-patrol`

The issue fences the scope hard: only `src/evaluator/` and its unit tests may
change. Nothing under `docs/testing/` may be touched at all - its `.ros` files,
`scenario.json` and `README.md` are the specification.

What the scenario demands, in one sentence: a condition on the configured points
budget (`field="limit::ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249"`) must read that budget even when the
condition carries `scope="force"`, instead of failing closed with an
`UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` diagnostic. Three of the scenario's four cases are red
today (rosters 01, 02, 03); roster 04 is green and must stay green.

## Changes expected

- `src/evaluator/query.js` - the query primitive and the **only** place that
  resolves a `limit::<costTypeId>` field; `resolveLimitValue` (around line 229)
  turns every scope other than `roster` into the `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` sentinel plus
  a diagnostic, and the same file already resolves the `force` frame for counting
  scopes (around line 172), so both halves of the question live here.
- `src/evaluator/model.js` - the shared vocabulary: the `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET`
  sentinel, `CountedFieldKind.LIMIT_VALUE`, `DiagnosticKind`, `ScopeKeyword` and
  `BudgetLimitUnresolvedReason` whose `NON_ROSTER_SCOPE` member and doc block
  encode exactly the rule the scenario contradicts.
- `src/evaluator/query.limitValue.test.js` - the unit test that pins today's rule;
  its `ScopeKeyword.FORCE` case (around line 85) asserts the diagnostic the
  scenario forbids.
- `src/evaluator/rosterBudget.js` - the roster-wide budget a `limit::` read
  resolves against, including its unlimited (`-1`) fail-closed path; whether a
  force frame needs anything of it is decided here.
- `src/evaluator/rosterBudget.unlimitedSentinel.test.js` - pins the unlimited
  budget's fail-closed resolution through a `limit::` read, so it moves with any
  change to how such a read resolves.

## Possibly involved - to confirm or rule out

- `src/evaluator/modifiers.js` - the consumer on the scenario's own path: the
  `set 1` modifier's condition fails closed on the `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` sentinel
  (around lines 172, 207, 229, 331), which is why the raised minimum is dead code
  today.
- `src/evaluator/constraints.js` - the other sentinel consumer (percent
  denominator, suspended limit; around lines 52, 93, 129) and the place where a
  limit's own `roster`/`force` scope is already distinguished.
- `src/evaluator/catalogReader.js` - reads `field="limit::<id>"` into
  `LIMIT_VALUE` and reads the condition's `scope` attribute; only involved if the
  gap turns out to be in the reading rather than the resolution.
- `src/evaluator/violationClassification.js` - maps `LIMIT_VALUE` onto a limit
  measure and classifies the diagnostics the report carries.
- `src/evaluator/report.js` - projects diagnostics and slot values
  (`effectiveMin`, `current`, `effectiveMax`, `headroom`, `isBlocked`) that the
  scenario pins per roster.
- `src/evaluator/enumHandlerCoverage.test.js`,
  `src/evaluator/violationClassification.test.js` - enumerate the enums above and
  will need a line if a diagnostic reason is added, renamed or removed.
- `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md` - the suite doc; a line only if a new test file is
  added to the directory.

## Read-only, never edited

- `docs/testing/equal-to-force-points-limit-border-patrol/` (`scenario.json`,
  `rosters/*.ros`, `README.md`) - the specification, explicitly out of scope.
- `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js` - the manifest-driven runner that turns
  every scenario under `docs/testing/` into cases; it is the check, never an edit.
- `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` - the frozen catalog data the
  scenario is derived from (the entry `2066-082d-a465-4baf` lives in
  `Mercenaries (6th definitive edition).cat`).
- `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` - the campaign driver's state; it pins this
  gap and lies outside the issue's fence, so the human moves it from `pinnedGaps`
  to closed when the campaign branch merges.
- `docs/evaluator-architecture.md` - describes the query primitive's contract
  (SS4.5, and the `LIMIT_VALUE` line around 170) and is already stale from earlier
  rounds; outside the fence, so it stays for the human to schedule.

increments.title: A budget-limit condition resolves in the force frame instead of failing closed
increments.goal: Make `docs/testing/equal-to-force-points-limit-border-patrol` green in all four of its cases. A condition reading the configured points budget (`field="limit::ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249"`) with `scope="force"` must resolve to the roster's configured budget - a `.ros` declares its budget only at the roster root, so a resolvable force frame yields exactly that number - instead of raising `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` and suspending its consumer. That makes the catalog author's rule live: at a budget of exactly 500 the `equalTo 500` gate holds and the `set 1` modifier raises the entry's own minimum (`1a97-1579-ab05-a6d7`) so the occupied slot reports `effectiveMin` 1, while 499 and 501 leave it at the base 0 with no diagnostic. This is the whole of the issue's first acceptance criterion; the second one - every scenario green today stays green - is a constraint on it, not separate work.
criteria: `npx vitest run src/evaluator` passes the cases `Szenario: equal-to-force-points-limit-border-patrol > rosters/01-budget-500-selected-min-raised.ros`, `> rosters/02-budget-499-selected-min-unraised.ros` and `> rosters/03-budget-501-selected-min-unraised.ros`.

In roster 01 the slot for defId `2066-082d-a465-4baf` with anchorKind `occupied` reports `effectiveMin` 1, `current` 1, `effectiveMax` 1, `headroom` 0, `isHidden` false and `isBlocked` true; in rosters 02 and 03 the same slot reports `effectiveMin` 0 with the rest unchanged.

No `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` diagnostic is raised in any of the four rosters, and the limits pinned `absent` by the scenario stay silent while the Core limit `35c2-d478-392a-aeb1` keeps firing with actual 0 against bound 2 in all four.
Roster `04-budget-500-unselected-no-anchor.ros` stays green: the raised minimum `1a97-1579-ab05-a6d7` still produces no anchor and stays silent.

A budget-limit read that genuinely cannot resolve - an unbudgeted cost type, an unlimited (`-1`) budget, or a frame the query cannot resolve - still fails closed with its diagnostic rather than silently answering 0; the unit tests that pin this are kept or replaced by equivalents, never weakened to let the scenario pass.
`npx vitest run src/evaluator` ends at exit 0 with no failure anywhere: every scenario the earlier rounds closed included, and no unit test of the evaluator suite skipped or deleted to get there.
Nothing outside `src/evaluator/` and its unit tests changes; no file under `docs/testing/` is touched.

# What gets built

One rule changes: a `limit::<costTypeId>` read (`CountedFieldKind.LIMIT_VALUE`) resolves in the **force** frame as well as the **roster** frame, and yields the same configured budget in both. Everything else about the read - the `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` sentinel, the `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` diagnostic, and every consumer's fail-closed handling - stays as it is.

Only two production files change: `src/evaluator/model.js` and `src/evaluator/query.js`.

## 1. `src/evaluator/model.js` - the reason vocabulary

`BudgetLimitUnresolvedReason` (model.js:93-100) today has two members. It gets three:

- `NOT_BUDGETED: 'notBudgeted'` - unchanged. The cost type is not in the budget. `createRosterBudget` drops an unlimited (`-1`) cost limit (rosterBudget.js:53-58), so the unlimited case keeps falling into exactly this branch - do not add a member for it.
- `NON_ROSTER_SCOPE` is renamed to `UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE: 'unsupportedScope'` - the scope is neither `roster` nor `force`. The old name states the rule this increment removes; keeping it would leave the vocabulary lying about itself. The rename is contained: the only readers are `query.js` and `query.limitValue.test.js` (nothing in `src/` outside `src/evaluator/` mentions it, and no scenario under `docs/testing/` pins a reason string - the scenarios pin only `kind`).
- `UNRESOLVED_FRAME: 'unresolvedFrame'` is added - the scope is `force` but the node has no enclosing force, so there is no frame to read a budget for. Distinct from `UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE` because the scope is supported and the *data* is what fails.

Update the doc block above the enum (it says "zwei distinkte Ursachen") and the `DiagnosticKind.UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` comment (model.js:549-553, it says "einen Scope ungleich `roster`").

Nothing else in the engine switches on a reason: `violationClassification.js` classifies by `kind` only, and `enumHandlerCoverage.test.js` enumerates comparators, condition-group combinators and modifier handlers - not diagnostic reasons. Adding a member breaks no coverage test.

## 2. `src/evaluator/query.js` - `resolveLimitValue` (query.js:219-248)

New shape of the function, in this order:

1. `scope === ScopeKeyword.ROSTER` -> budget lookup (step 4).
2. `scope === ScopeKeyword.FORCE` -> the frame is `ctx.node.forceRoot`. If it is `null`/`undefined`, push `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` with `reason: UNRESOLVED_FRAME` (detail: `costTypeId`, `scope`) and return `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET`. Otherwise fall through to the budget lookup - the frame node itself is not read for anything else.
3. any other scope (`parent`, `self`, `unit`, `ancestor`, `primary-catalogue`, an entry or category ID) -> `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` plus `reason: UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE` (detail: `costTypeId`, `scope`), exactly as today.
4. budget lookup, unchanged: `ctx.budget.get(costTypeId)`; `undefined` -> `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` plus `reason: NOT_BUDGETED`; otherwise the number.

The order matters and is pinned by tests: an unresolvable force frame is reported as `UNRESOLVED_FRAME` even when the cost type is budgeted, and a resolvable force frame over an unbudgeted cost type is reported as `NOT_BUDGETED`.

The resolution stays **independent of the flags**, like `primary-catalogue` (query.js:250-310): `query` answers a `LIMIT_VALUE` field before `normalizeFlags`/`resolveFrame` ever run (query.js:371-376), and `shared="false"` does not make a configured budget narrower. Do not route `LIMIT_VALUE` through `resolveFrame`.

Update the JSDoc of `resolveLimitValue` and the module header paragraph (query.js:15-21) that calls `limit::<costTypeId>` a non-counting frame - it still is, but the sentence "ein Scope ungleich `roster` wird nicht still umgedeutet" must become "ein Scope ausserhalb von `roster`/`force`".

## Why the force frame yields the roster budget

A `.ros` declares `<costLimits>` only at the `<roster>` root; the format knows no place where a single `<force>` sets its own cost limit (bsdata reference SS5.6/SS7.6, and the engine facade takes one flat list: `createRosterBudget(roster.costLimits)`, evaluator.js:224). A force therefore lies in exactly one roster and its configured limit *is* that roster's. That is why step 2 falls through to the same lookup rather than inventing a per-force budget. The same pairing already exists one layer up: `countingFlagsOf` in constraints.js:91-98 treats `ROSTER` and `FORCE` as the two frame keywords a limit can carry.

The catalog data agree: in the frozen fixture corpus `field="limit::..."` occurs 81 times with `scope="roster"` and exactly once with `scope="force"` - the condition of this scenario (`Mercenaries (6th definitive edition).cat:9387`). The `.gst` uses `scope="roster"` for the same quantity throughout, so both spellings must answer the same number.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Resolve `LIMIT_VALUE` for every scope** ("the budget is frame-independent, so answer it always"). Rejected: with `shared="false"` and with `parent`/`self`/`unit` every read would resolve, and the increment's fifth criterion demands that a frame the query cannot resolve still fails closed. It also throws away a guard for scopes the corpus never exercises.
- **Route `LIMIT_VALUE` through `resolveFrame`.** Rejected: that function carries the `shared` rule and the category-target widening (query.js:204-217), none of which mean anything for a budget, and it would silently resolve `parent`/`self`/`unit` as above.
- **Let the consumers treat the sentinel as "holds"** (modifiers.js:207, constraints.js:129). Rejected: that inverts fail-closed for *every* unresolvable budget, including the `orcs-and-goblins-budget` roster 06 case that pins the diagnostic.
- **A new diagnostic kind for the force case.** Rejected: the scenario pins the absence of `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT`, and a second kind for the same failure would split what a report reader has to look for. A reason member is the established way to split causes (`CatalogueUnreadableReason` does the same).

## Blast radius

- The gated entry `2066-082d-a465-4baf` appears in no scenario other than `equal-to-force-points-limit-border-patrol`, and no `entryLink` in the corpus points at it - so nothing outside those rosters starts evaluating it.
- `orcs-and-goblins-budget` roster 06 (the only scenario that pins the diagnostic as *present*) reads `limit::` with `scope="roster"` and has no `<costLimits>` -> still `NOT_BUDGETED`, still fires.
- Synthetic nodes carry their owner's `forceRoot` (evalTree.js:891), so an offer anchor or mandatory phantom inside a force resolves like a real selection; the tree root carries `forceRoot: null` (evalTree.js:1002) and keeps failing closed.
- After the change, roster 01's condition holds, the `set 1` raises constraint `1a97-1579-ab05-a6d7` from min 0 to min 1, and the occupied slot's `effectiveMin` comes from that bound (report.js:441). Current 1 >= 1, so the limit stays satisfied and silent - which is what the scenario pins.

## Already red, without running anything

I ran no command. From the issue and the scenario file: the three cases `Szenario: equal-to-force-points-limit-border-patrol > rosters/01-...`, `> 02-...` and `> 03-...` fail today; roster 04 passes. No unit test is red today - but `src/evaluator/query.limitValue.test.js` contains a case ("meldet einen Scope ungleich roster als Diagnose statt stiller Umdeutung", lines 80-95) that pins exactly the rule this increment removes, so it turns red the moment the production change lands and must be rewritten in this step. Leave the first run of the check list to whoever runs it downstream.

## Criterion 1 - the scenario goes green

Covered by the committed scenario through `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js`. **Write nothing for it**: the scenario and the runner are both out of scope, and `npx vitest run src/evaluator` executes them.

## Criterion 2 - the force frame resolves, and only where it can

Level: unit. File: `src/evaluator/query.limitValue.test.js` (existing). Framework: vitest. Command: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/query.limitValue.test.js`.

The file's `contextWithBudget` helper builds `node: { isRoot: true }` with no `forceRoot`; extend it (or add a sibling helper) so a case can choose the node's `forceRoot`. Keep `forbiddenIndex` in every case - a `LIMIT_VALUE` read must still never touch the count index.

Keep unchanged (they are the fail-closed guard the fifth criterion protects):

1. roster scope, budgeted cost type -> the number, no diagnostic.
2. roster scope, `childId="any"` -> same number (the target ID is ignored).
3. roster scope, cost type not budgeted -> `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` plus `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` / `NOT_BUDGETED`.
4. a `COST_SUM` field still reads the (forbidden) index and throws.

Rewrite case 5 (today's `ScopeKeyword.FORCE` case) and add the rest:

5. **force scope, node with a non-null `forceRoot`, cost type budgeted** -> the configured number, `diagnostics` empty. This is the case the scenario needs; red before the production change.
6. **force scope, node with `forceRoot: null`** (the frame the query cannot resolve) -> `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET`, and a diagnostic `{ kind: UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT, costTypeId, reason: UNRESOLVED_FRAME, scope: 'force' }`. Budget the cost type in this case, so the failure is provably the frame and not the lookup.
7. **a scope that is neither roster nor force** -> `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` plus reason `UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`. Use `ScopeKeyword.PARENT` for one case and one more spelling (`ScopeKeyword.SELF`, `ScopeKeyword.UNIT` or an entry ID as scope) for a second, so the branch is pinned as a rule and not as one keyword. This case replaces the deleted one; without it the read could silently answer 0 for any scope.
8. **force scope, resolvable frame, cost type not budgeted** -> `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET` plus `NOT_BUDGETED` (not `UNRESOLVED_FRAME`). Pins the order of the two checks.
9. **force scope with `shared: false`** and a resolvable frame -> the configured number. Pins that the read is independent of the flags.

Level: unit. File: `src/evaluator/rosterBudget.unlimitedSentinel.test.js` (existing). Command: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/rosterBudget.unlimitedSentinel.test.js`.

10. Add **one** case beside the existing roster-scope one: an unlimited (`-1`) cost limit read with `scope="force"` at a node with a resolvable `forceRoot` -> `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET`, never the number `-1`, plus an `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` diagnostic (assert `kind` and `costTypeId`; leave the exact reason open, as the file's sibling case already does). Change no existing case in this file.

## Criterion 3 - the gate is live end to end

Level: facade (`prepareDataset` + `evaluate`), synthetic catalogue, no fixture. New file: `src/evaluator/query.limitValueForceScope.test.js`. Command: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/query.limitValueForceScope.test.js`.

This duplicates part of the scenario on purpose: the scenario is black-box authorship that may move or be re-pinned by the campaign, and the engine needs its own fixture-free regression guard for the whole path (catalogue reader -> condition -> `set` modifier -> constraint -> report). Keep it to three cases.

The catalogue rebuilds the scenario's construction in miniature: a `forceEntry`; one selectable `selectionEntry` (`type="upgrade"`, `hidden="false"`) with a `constraint type="min" value="0" field="selections" scope="parent"` carrying an id, and a `modifier type="set" value="1"` on that constraint id whose single condition is `type="equalTo" value="500" field="limit::<PTS>" scope="force" childId="any" shared="true" includeChildSelections="true" includeChildForces="true"`. The roster is built inline as `{ costLimits: [{ costTypeId: PTS, value: <n> }], forces: [{ defId: FORCE, count: 1, children: [{ defId: ENTRY, count: 1, children: [] }] }] }` - the shape `evaluate` documents (evaluator.js:113-116) and the shape `modifiers.setWithRepeat.test.js` and `constraints.hiddenMin.test.js` already use.

11. Budget exactly 500 -> the occupied slot of the entry reports `effectiveMin` 1, and `report.diagnostics` contains no `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT`.
12. Budget 499 -> the same slot reports `effectiveMin` 0, still no `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` (`equalTo` is not `atMost`, and the resolved read produces no diagnostic).
13. Roster **without** `costLimits` -> the same slot reports `effectiveMin` 0 **and** an `UNRESOLVED_BUDGET_LIMIT` diagnostic is present. This is the end-to-end half of "a read that genuinely cannot resolve still fails closed".

Read the slot as `[...report.capabilities.values()].find(c => c.defId === ENTRY && c.anchorKind === 'occupied')` (the projection is `report.js` `toCapability`; `modifiers.setWithRepeat.test.js` shows the lookup pattern).

Adding this file makes the count in `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md` ("73 of the 85 test files") stale; correct both numbers there. That doc is otherwise accurate and does not contradict anything I read - it covers this directory's conventions and explicitly excludes the manifest runner.

## Left untested, on purpose

- `scope="force"` yielding a value *different* from `scope="roster"`: the `.ros` format has no per-force cost limit, so no roster can distinguish them. The scenario's README states the same gap.
- The remaining non-force scopes beyond the two spellings in case 7: they are one branch, and a third spelling buys nothing.
- The reason string in the report projection: nothing in the engine switches on a `BudgetLimitUnresolvedReason`, so there is no consumer to pin.
- Roster 04 of the scenario (no anchor for an unreferenced shared entry): already green and owned by the scenario runner; no unit test restates it.

## What counts as done

`npx vitest run src/evaluator`, from the repository root. That single command runs the evaluator unit suite and the manifest-driven scenario runner; its exit code judges the work. Nothing else is run.
return.summary: Researched the force-scoped budget-limit gap: the fix is `resolveLimitValue` in `src/evaluator/query.js` accepting `scope="force"` by resolving `ctx.node.forceRoot` and reading the same roster-wide budget, with a third `BudgetLimitUnresolvedReason` in `model.js` for a force frame that does not resolve, so unbudgeted, unlimited (`-1`) and frameless reads keep failing closed. The test plan rewrites the obsolete case in `query.limitValue.test.js`, adds force-frame cases there and in `rosterBudget.unlimitedSentinel.test.js`, and adds a fixture-free facade file `query.limitValueForceScope.test.js`; the check is `npx vitest run src/evaluator`.
